desc: Formalize the model: valid placements = edge subsets of the torus grid where every used A-cell is a turn (adjacent edges), every used B-cell is straight (opposite edges), all other cells degree 0; i.e., unions of vertex-disjoint cycles that turn exactly at A-cells and go straight exactly at B-cells (equivalently: orthogonal polygons whose corners are A-cells and whose straight segments pass only through B-cells, plus full all-B rows/columns wrapping the torus).

Build a brute-force enumerator for tiny grids (H,W ≤ 3) over all patterns and placements; confirm the reformulation and collect answer data (sanity: all-B must give 2^H + 2^W − 1; samples give 2, 0, 2).

Run brute force on all patterns for H,W ≤ 3 (plus selected 2×4/3×4); verify all-B = 2^H+2^W−1 and samples = 2,0,2; tabulate answers and test factorization hypotheses (powers of 2, products over components, correlation with A-corner rectangles / B-only straight segments).

Based on data, pin down the exact structural theorem: candidate directions are (a) billiard/reflection orbits on directed edges giving per-orbit binary choices, (b) decomposition into independent "forced" components via a derived graph on rows/columns/diagonals, (c) global case split between contractible cycles (rectangles/polygons with A-corners) and non-contractible all-B rows/columns; determine the precise counting formula and prove it.
Implement the final algorithm at O(HW) (or O(HW α)) per test case with fast I/O (T ≤ 1e5, total cells ≤ 1e6), mod 998244353.

Validate the final implementation against the brute-force enumerator on all tiny grids and random small grids; check edge cases (H=2 or W=2 wrap-around quirks, all-A grids, single valid configuration, answer 0); write up proof of correctness and complexity.
